questions.q: What question does the Dev environment answer?
options: Does this work at all?
Is this what the business actually wanted?
Is this safe enough to bet the business on?
Does this work correctly in every edge case?
questions.explain: Dev is the developer's own workspace where a change is written and debugged — it answers the most basic question, whether the change works at all.

questions.q: QA and UAT both involve testing a change before release. What's the key difference between what each one checks?
options: QA checks whether the change works correctly including edge cases; UAT checks whether it's actually what the business asked for
QA and UAT check exactly the same thing, so one is redundant
QA is done by the business; UAT is done by developers
UAT happens before QA in every organization
questions.explain: QA answers 'does this work correctly, including cases the developer didn't think of?' while UAT answers a different question: 'is this what we actually wanted?' Code can be technically correct and still miss what the business needed.

questions.q: Where does Code Review happen in the chain shown in this lesson?
options: Inside the Dev stage, before the change is merged to QA
After Production, as a final audit
During UAT, performed by the business
Code review isn't part of this chain at all
questions.explain: Code Review sits inside the Dev stage — a teammate reviews the pull request's approach and correctness before the change is even merged to QA.

questions.q: A junior engineer says, 'It works on my machine, why can't it go live?' What's the problem with that reasoning?
options: "Works on my machine" has only answered Dev's question — none of QA's, UAT's, or Production's questions have been answered yet
There's no problem — if it works on one machine, it will work everywhere
The engineer should skip straight to UAT, bypassing QA entirely
Production doesn't actually require passing through any prior stage
questions.explain: Dev only confirms the change works at all. QA, UAT, and Production each ask a different question that Dev alone can't answer — correctness under edge cases, business acceptance, and production-readiness, respectively.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's true about Production?
options: Nothing reaches Production until it has cleared every environment before it
Production is optional for most companies
Production and Dev are the same environment in most organizations
Production never needs a prior QA or UAT pass if the developer is confident
questions.explain: Production is the real, live system real users depend on — the entire point of the DEV → QA → UAT → PROD chain is that nothing reaches Production until it has passed every stage before it.
